blocks.content: A complementary graph (G‾ \overline{G} G) is defined as a graph that contains the same vertices of the original graph (G) such that

items: if two vertices are connected in G, they are not connected in G‾ \overline{G} G.
if two vertices are not connected in G, they are connected in G‾ \overline{G} G.

blocks.content: The above figure shows graph G and its complementary graph G‾ \overline{G} G.
Complementary graphs are used to represent the inverse or missing relationships between vertices in a given graph.
